newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close much stronger on U.S. gains.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close much stronger on U.S. gains.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Friday, driven by gains in U.S. treasuries, which rallied unexpectedly after a strong U.S. employment report, analysts said.

"The general direction is obviously from the U.S.," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian fixed-income analyst with New York-based I.D.E.A. "Once the move began, it just started triggering stops and it gathered steam."
Canada's 30-year benchmark rose C$1.82 to C$114.20 to yield 6.875 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 1-7/32 to yield 6.78 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to 10 basis points from 13 basis points on Thursday.

Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets weakened after the U.S. Labor Department reported that 138,000 jobs were created in May and that the unemployment rate fell to 4.8 percent. The data initially prompted fears that the Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee would hike rates in July.
But U.S. treasuries rebounded amid foreign and retail buying and a wave of short covering by traders who had set positions ahead of the employment data.
The short-covering rally was mirrored in Canada, where volumes were lighter in the afternoon than in the morning, said one bond trader with a bank-owned brokerage.
"It was just a matter of bad short scrambling," said the trader.

In economic news, Statistics Canada reported this morning that employment rose by 61,300 jobs in May, well above expectations of a 34,700 increase. The unemployment rate fell to 9.5 percent from 9.6 percent in April.
The Canadian employment report was largely overshadowed by the U.S. job reports and the bond market activity there.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.93 to C$106.49 to yield 6.361 percent while the U.S. 10-year rose 27/32 to 6.50 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds was 14 basis points, unchanged from Thursday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.88 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.05 percent.
